text.p: These are the main stories in Slovenia's Friday morning newspapers:
- Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler has resigned over divisions among Slovenia's political parties. He will keep the post until September when the government is expected to name a new foreign minister.
- The government said citizens will still be able to use privatisation vouchers, which expired at the end of June, to purchase shares in the company where they work.
- Parliament held its last session before the summer recess on Thursday and will reassemble in September.
- The monthly inflation rate rose to one percent in July compared to 0.4 percent in June.
- The contolling board of supermarket group Nama decided to change the group's management whose mandate expired on Wednesday.

- The controlling board of trader Mercator said it might bring back the previous management board if it prepared a sound programme for changes in the company by mid-August. The previous management board was ejected last week.
- Parliament will debate a law on partial privatisation of Slovenia's Ironworks in September.
- The delay in passing the 1997 budget proposal, which was adopted by the government on Monday, may harm Slovenia's economy, experts said.

- Slovenia's basic interest rate, which is calculated according to inflation in the past 12 months, rose to 0.8 percent in August from 0.7 percent in July after monthly inflation rose to one percent in July.
